evidence.quote: The micron-size dark regions along the extrusion direction are icosahedral phase.
a ternary quasicrystalline icosahedral phase Mg42Zn50RE8 exists in equilibrium with a-Mg
In addition, there was a distribution of fine particles of icosahedral phase
The shape of nanoscale icosahedral particles in the Mg96.9Zn2.7Ho0.4 alloy are mostly rod-shaped (Fig. 2), while those in the Mg93Zn6Ho alloy are more varied.
There were also nanosized precipitates of monoclinic Mg4Zn7 phase in the matrix.
The Mg96.9Zn2.7Ho0.4 alloy has a comparatively much stronger texture, but is weak in comparison with common magnesium alloys.
It is observed that the Mg93Zn6Ho alloy has an extremely weak texture.
The high resolution micrograph shows a coherency at the interface.
Figure 4 shows grain misorientation angles for the two alloys with same average grain size of 1.3 lm. A remarkable similarity is observed here
In tension, the YSs for the alloy extruded at 260 and 300 °C are close to 200 MPa.
In tension, the YSs for the alloy extruded at 260 and 300 °C are close to 200 MPa.
The YS is dramatically increased to about 300 MPa on extrusion at 210 °C.
Elongations are 15–20%.
Compressive YSs range from 160 to 300 MPa.
Remarkably, in this alloy extruded at 230 °C the compressive YS (>300 MPa) is higher than the tensile (>280 MPa).

As is characteristic of magnesium alloys in compression, a stress plateau occurs after yielding, indicating twinning.
